messages:
Laura: heads-up — p99 in us-west-2 jumped ~2.5x at 14:12 UTC, customer-reported latency spikes for chat endpoints. Seeing a big drop in KV hit rate on the dashboard.
Ravi: looking now — there was a prefix-gc sweep started at 14:11 by maintenance job `prefix-gc-v2`. Logs show ~1.2M keys evicted in a 30s window. KV hit rate fell 97% -> 43% at same time.
Ashley: ouch. That will definitely blow up p95/p99 if clients hit cold prefixes. Can we pause the sweep? Any quick mitigations? :eyes:
Ravi: pausing is my recommendation. I can flip the job to `paused` for 20m from infra console. Also throttling the eviction loop to 100k keys/min would help.
Mike: repro steps in case teams want to test locally: run the attached warmup script against a small dev cluster to simulate high-entropy session prefixes, then run a forced gc. Example: 
```
# generate hot prefixes
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do curl -s "http://dev-kv.local/write?prefix=session-$RANDOM" >/dev/null & done
# force GC (dev-only)
curl -X POST http://dev-kv.local/admin/force-prefix-gc
```
You should see hit-rate collapse if your warmup is naive.
Olivia: long-term fixes we discussed in design review: soft-ttl per-tenant, staggered GC windows with jitter, and a quick-path for warmup drip (n-per-second rehydrate) instead of bulk rehydration. Also consider LFU-like eviction for prefix keys instead of pure LRU to keep session hotkeys.
Laura: for immediate customer relief — Ravi, please pause the job; Ashley, please update the routing policy to prefer dedicated pool for the affected tenant for the next 30m (reduce surface). Mike, post the repro in the support ticket so SEs can validate.
Ravi: paused prefix-gc at 14:20 UTC. Rolling throttle change to 100k/min queued. Confirmed eviction rate down in metrics, hit-rate climbing slowly.
Ashley: routing rule applied for tenant `acme-inc` at 14:23 UTC to dedicated-usw2-fallback. :white_check_mark:
Mike: added repro script + sample wrk command to support ticket #SUP-4592. Suggests we add an automated smoke after GC runs to detect hit-rate collapse and auto-halt.
Olivia: note for backlog: implement GC hysteresis (do not evict >X% of keys in Ts window), add random shard offsets to avoid cluster-wide simultaneous sweeps, and expose per-tenant GC safety valves.
Ravi: logs excerpt (sanitized):
```
[I] 2026-03-17T14:11:05Z prefix-gc-v2: started sweep
[I] 2026-03-17T14:11:40Z prefix-gc-v2: evicted=1203478 duration_ms=35012 rate=34454/s
[W] 2026-03-17T14:11:45Z kv-metrics: hit_rate=0.43 prev=0.97 tenant=acme-inc
```
Laura: tl;dr: immediate pause + throttling helped bring p99 down, add automatic stop condition to GC, and schedule follow-up to implement staggered/jittered windows. I'll own the follow-up ticket and triage with product for per-tenant controls.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-1123 created (priority: high) — assigned: Ravi, Ashley, Olivia, Mike, Laura.
Ashley: quick checklist posted to the incident thread: pause job, route affected tenant, notify SEs, collect spectrum traces, run repro in staging, plan code-level fixes.
Laura: thanks team. I'll post a short postmortem draft in #postmortems once we have metrics for the 2-hour window.
